newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Gains to VSZ shares drive Slovak bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Gains to VSZ shares drive Slovak bourse higher.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed steady in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, with gains to shares of steel producer VSZ boosting the SAX index 1.74 points to 207.64.
VSZ gained 15 crowns to close at 730, and brokers said the company's good fundamentals and continuing foreign interest in the issue give the shares potential to rise further.

"A package of as much as 200,000 shares may have been sold abroad, and maybe the buyers will want to collect more outstanding stocks from the market...so the share could go even higher," said Radovan Dzugas of Creditanstalt.
Analysts said a realistic market price for VSZ could be as high as 900 crowns, when compared to similar producers in the region.

Brokers said the general sluggish sentiment on the world markets now appears to have inflitrated the Slovak bourse, putting many foreign investors on the sidelines as they await a stronger impulse to show the bourse's future trend.

Oil refiner Slovnaft closed unchanged at its nominal value of 1,000 crowns and Dzugas said the issue was still undervalued, with a larger parcel of Slovnaft shares could be available at about 1,050 crowns.
Drug producer Slovakofarma continued to be plagued with low liquidity, trading only 26 shares on Thursday, but lasting strong demand again pushed the price higher -- by 21 crowns to 5,121.
Overall volume rose to 895,453 shares, boosted mainly by direct trades, from 254,837 stocks on Wednesday. Turnover fell to 184.25 crowns, from 210.27 million on Wednesday.
